chunk_findings.detail: `_apply` raises `InvalidValue` for every committed `file` value of `agent.roles` / `agent.capability_verbs`, including a table that only restates the shipped default or narrows a role. Given a project config whose `[agent].roles` is `{"operator": ["*"], "bot": ["read"]}` (tighter than the default bot list, and the write path the knob docstring still documents as `ddflow config --set agent.roles ...` without `--local`), load does not keep the layer below — it aborts that knob with an operator-only error. chunk_findings.detail: `_widens_verb_table` treats a grant as held only by exact string membership, and only the bare token `"*"` short-circuits. `[agent].capability_verbs` is documented to allow globs such as `gate *`. Given a lower layer `{"approve_marked": ["gate *"]}` and a committed file value `{"approve_marked": ["gate status"]}`, line 100 evaluates `"gate status" <= {"gate *"}` as false and returns True, so `_operator_only_refusal` raises `InvalidValue`. That committed table does not grant any verb the glob did not already hold; it is a tightening (r-tighten-only), and config load wrongly rejects it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_held` treats a committed grant as already authorized when the grant’s text matches a below fnmatch pattern, not when every verb that grant expands to was already held. The old `*` check required the below layer to contain the every-capability token; the new code does not. Given below `{"approve_marked": ["?"]}` (only single-character verbs) and a committed file value `{"approve_marked": ["*"]}`, `fnmatch.fnmatchcase("*", "?")` is True, so `_widens_verb_table` returns False and `_operator_only_refusal` allows the file layer. That committed `*` grants every verb, not the one-character set `?` already held. The same hole admits `{"approve_marked": ["?*"]}` against below `["??"]`: the two-character pattern matches the text `?*`, whose language is every non-empty verb.
